raw.assessment: The incumbent already produces usable exports with seven-minute median handling for 24 unchanged-assignment files, supporting retention of its private, center-scoped CSV path. Overall intended-course coverage was 32/40 (80%) and median handling 17 minutes. Assignment changes coincide with six affected exports but do not establish causation. The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only explanation. Short job execution and long replacement waits suggest a separate coordination delay, whose cause is unmeasured. Zero observed cross-center rows does not establish isolation for the omitted split-course center. Coordinator checking and spreadsheet import costs remain unobserved.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignments for historical weeks may exclude intended courses; week-relevant selection could reduce assignment-associated corrections.
openings.delta: Locate a possible error in course selection before changing the scheduler or CSV format.
openings.prediction: With identical fabricated attendance and requested week, changing only the current assignment changes incumbent course inclusion; a week-relevant rule retains the coordinator-agreed course set.
openings.probe: In private staging, compare unchanged and midweek-transfer fixtures, then a split-course fixture with distinct center assignments. Agree expected sets with coordinators first. Compare course membership and center ownership under current and candidate rules while attendance entry continues. Preserve the documented CSV schema; estimate implementation within six engineer-days and existing hosting before choosing a change.
assumptions: Week-relevant membership can be defined unambiguously.
Historical assignment data availability is unknown; fabricated fixtures test behavior, not production feasibility.

openings.claim: Were renamed courses absent from the export, or present under names that failed coordinator reconciliation?
openings.delta: Distinguish selection failure from naming or timetable mismatch in the concrete counterexample to assignment-only repair.
openings.prediction: A reconciliation mismatch retains the expected internal course identity and participant rows but produces a missing-course report; selection failure lacks those rows before spreadsheet import.
openings.probe: Use fabricated rename cases in the six coordinators' short sessions. Compare internal course identities with agreed intended sets and observe checking and import separately. Keep the CSV unchanged and all participant material in private staging or authorized workspaces; bound this diagnostic before implementation.
assumptions: Fabricated sessions approximate real checking sufficiently to discriminate these mechanisms.

raw.assessment: Assignment changes and renames are associated with affected exports, but causes remain unestablished. Two counterfactual alternatives warrant bounded tests; neither has demonstrated the outcome or six-day feasibility.

openings.claim: Forbid current instructor assignment as the dependency determining course inclusion. Instead, export a center/week manifest of stable course identifiers confirmed by its coordinator, retrieving attendance independently of current instructor ownership.
openings.delta: Course inclusion depends on an explicit intended set rather than present instructor assignment or matching course names.
openings.prediction: With identical attendance and manifest, changing only current instructor assignment or course label leaves included course identifiers unchanged; coordinator confirmation may offset any checking-time savings.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging, compare incumbent and manifest exports under assignment changes, renames, and a split. Have six coordinators specify intended sets before inspecting output; measure total handling including manifest preparation. Reject on foreign-center rows or blocked attendance entry; estimate effort before implementation.
assumptions: Replacement dependencies: stable course identifiers and explicit split mappings; retrievable course/week attendance independent of current instructor; accurate coordinator manifest and usable selection interface; authenticated center-scoped retrieval; existing private hosting, nonblocking reads, and documented CSV serializer; implementation within six engineer-days and hosting allowance.

openings.claim: Forbid dependence on Sunday batch timing for file availability. Let an authorized coordinator request a center/week export when needed, using a bounded job in the existing service.
openings.delta: The coordinator controls generation timing and can regenerate directly after a correction.
openings.prediction: Direct requests shorten elapsed replacement waits if scheduling or handoff causes them; unchanged course-set errors would distinguish availability improvement from selection repair.
openings.probe: Time request, completion, download, checking, correction, and import separately in staged coordinator sessions. Compare direct generation with the incumbent path, measure ordinary attendance-write latency during concurrent requests, and verify center isolation and CSV compatibility.
assumptions: Replacement dependencies: authenticated center/week request interface; existing scoped generator; bounded concurrency and sufficient hosting headroom; private result storage and delivery; nonblocking attendance access; documented CSV output; engineering estimate within six days. Faster availability alone need not reduce active handling or improve course selection.

openings.claim: Current assignments may distort historical-week selection.
openings.probe: Agree intended sets; compare current/week-relevant rules on unchanged, transfer and cross-center split fixtures.
openings.uncertainty: Correlation only; historical data and week membership unresolved.

openings.claim: Rename complaints may be reconciliation failures.
openings.discriminator: Expected identities/rows present versus absent before import.
openings.probe: Observe six coordinators checking/importing fabricated rename cases against agreed sets.
openings.uncertainty: Identity visibility, timetable accuracy and session realism unknown.

openings.claim: Confirmed stable-ID manifests could control inclusion independently of assignments/labels.
openings.probe: Compare transfer, rename and split fixtures; count manifest preparation in handling.
openings.uncertainty: Needs accurate manifests, usable selection, stable IDs, split mappings and independently retrievable attendance; confirmation may erase savings.

openings.claim: Authorized direct requests could shorten replacement waits.
openings.discriminator: Wait improves while selection errors persist.
openings.probe: Compare request-to-use stages and concurrent attendance-write latency.
openings.uncertainty: Wait cause, concurrency/headroom unknown; faster availability need not improve handling/selection.

post_distill.decision: Keep incumbent pending fabricated private-staging probes; none proven. Preserve private/authorized participant handling and documented CSV. Reject foreign-center rows or blocked attendance entry, including split fixtures. Estimate six-day/hosting fit before implementation. Measure checking, correction, download and import separately; evaluate eventual exports against stipulated targets.
